drovr: stop calling gemma's review verdicts fabricated

The comment asserted that gemma-4-31b returns PASSes without reading the
diff, and concluded "a gemma PASS is unverified, not verified". That framing
is wrong: the reviews are real. A panel that returns in seconds is the model
being fast, not a reviewer skipping the work — and the comment as written
trains anyone reading it (human or agent) to throw away a legitimate clean
verdict on wall-clock alone.

Kept: why pi rather than opencode, why the model is pinned here, why the
table has to come last, and the glm-5.3 non-delivery measurement, which is a
fact about glm and not a claim about gemma. Also kept the note that drovr's
old delivery floor is gone (f016dcc) — it could not tell "did not read" from
"reads quickly" and rejected every review on a fast backend, which is the
same mistake in code form.

======
gvfs: link the systemd user units its D-Bus services activate through

be870dd put gvfs on PATH and pointed GIO_EXTRA_MODULES at it, which was
necessary and not sufficient. Verified after switching: the module loads and
finds all four monitors, the broker resolves their names once reloaded, and
then every one of them dies anyway.

The reason is that gvfs's D-Bus service files activate via SystemdService=
rather than Exec=, so the broker does not spawn the daemon itself -- it hands
the name to systemd, which has never heard of gvfs-udisks2-volume-monitor.service
because standalone home-manager does not put ~/.nix-profile/share/systemd/user
on the unit search path. This is the same trap the xdg portals sit in, three
stanzas up, with the same "unknown unit" in the error. The error moves through
two distinct shapes as you fix the earlier halves, which is worth knowing when
reading this back: ServiceUnknown ("not activatable") is the broker not knowing
the name, NameHasNoOwner ("unknown unit") is the broker knowing it and systemd
not.

All six units go in, not just udisks2. GIO probes every monitor that ships a
.monitor file in the package, so linking one and leaving the others out swaps
a missing drive for four IsSupported() failures on every enumeration. They are
D-Bus activated and stay idle until something asks for them.

withHostNss for the same reason the portals use it: it rewrites ExecStart= in
the unit to point at the NSS-wrapped libexec binary, so activation does not
land on a nix-glibc binary that cannot resolve host users.

git add home.nix && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git push -q origin master && git log -1 --oneline
claude: auto-approve cd into a drovr worktree

drovr runs work in a worktree at <repo>/.drovr/wt/<run>, so nearly every
command in a run opens with a `cd` into one. That is navigation inside the
repo the session is already working in, but the auto-mode classifier reads
an absolute `cd` out of the session cwd as leaving the project and prompts
for it, once per run, forever.

This has to be an autoMode.allow rule rather than a permissions.allow one.
Bash permission rules are exact-match or `:*`-prefix only -- there is no
mid-path wildcard, so "any repo's .drovr/wt" is inexpressible and the only
rule that would match is `Bash(cd:*)`, which allows every cd anywhere.

The rule is scoped to the directory change alone and says so, so a command
chained after the `cd` is still judged on its own merits. Classifier rules
compose that way; a PreToolUse hook returning permissionDecision "allow"
-- the one mechanism the drovr plugin itself could ship, since plugins
contribute hooks but not settings -- would not, because an allow decision
bypasses the permission check for the whole Bash call rather than for the
`cd` segment that earned it.

content.text:
Done — committed `ceb2d53`, pushed.

**Step 1 of 2 done: rule added.** Next: run `hms` to apply it (~10 min).

## What changed

`home.nix:1084` — an `autoMode.allow` rule (your settings.json is home-manager-generated, so the source is the nix file, not `~/.claude/settings.json`):

> Changing directory into a drovr worktree is ALLOWED: a `cd` whose target path contains `/.drovr/wt/`… Judge any command chained after the `cd` on its own merits.

It had to go in `autoMode.allow`, not `permissions.allow`: Bash permission rules are exact-match or `:*`-prefix only. There's no mid-path wildcard, so "any repo's `.drovr/wt`" is inexpressible — the only rule that would match is `Bash(cd:*)`, which allows every `cd` anywhere.

## Your question: can the drovr plugin do this?

**Partly — and you don't want it to.**

Plugins contribute skills, commands, agents, hooks, and MCP servers. They **cannot** contribute `permissions.allow` or `autoMode.allow`; those are settings-file-only. drovr's one lever is a `PreToolUse` hook on `Bash` returning `permissionDecision: "allow"` — it already ships `hooks/hooks.json` (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit), so adding one is mechanical.

The problem: an allow decision bypasses the permission check for the **entire Bash call**, not the `cd` segment that earned it. Real drovr usage is `cd <wt>\ngit commit ...` (multi-line), so the hook would have to either blanket-approve whatever follows the `cd`, or restrict itself to bare `cd` with nothing chained — which almost never happens, making it useless.

The classifier rule composes correctly instead: it clears the `cd` and still judges the rest.

**Next action (~10 min, blocks):** run `hms`.
